title: Stage 1: Start the feature
summary: 9:00. Pick up ticket SHOP-142, branch from a fresh main with the team's naming rule, and make focused commits.

steps.title: Your day
body: You are on the checkout team of an online shop. Five engineers, trunk-based: short-lived branches, pull requests into `main`, squash-merge, and a `release/3.1` branch for the version currently in production.
Today's ticket is **SHOP-142: Percentage coupons**. Over five stages the day will go like this:
2. A teammate pushes a change that conflicts with yours.
3. Clean up your commits with interactive rebase for review.
4. Production bug: backport a hotfix with cherry-pick.
5. Someone's commit vanishes; rescue it with the reflog.
Each stage ends in a real terminal: your own clone of the team's repo, with a bare `origin` standing in for GitHub and teammates who push while you work.

steps.prompt: Arrange your first commands of the day, starting the branch from the newest `main`.
steps.explain: Always branch from an up-to-date `main`; otherwise you start with an old base and buy yourself conflicts. `git status -s` confirms you start clean.

steps.prompt: You edited `Coupon.cs` (new file) and `Cart.cs`, plus fixed an unrelated typo in `README.md`. You staged only `Coupon.cs` and the coupon hunk of `Cart.cs` with `git add -p`. What does `git status -s` print? (Name order, untracked last.)
code: git add -p Cart.cs     # staged the coupon hunk; one unrelated hunk left
steps.explain: `Cart.cs` has a staged hunk and an unstaged one: `MM`. The README typo is unstaged. `Coupon.cs` was added, so it is no longer untracked.

steps.prompt: The README typo fix is unrelated to the coupon work. What should happen to it?
options: Commit it separately (or in its own small PR), so the coupon commit stays one logical change
Include it in the coupon commit to save time
steps.explain: Mixed commits make review, revert and cherry-pick harder. One change, one commit.

steps.prompt: Complete the commands: commit the staged coupon work, then publish the branch and set its upstream.
steps.explain: `-a` would have swept the unrelated `Cart.cs` hunk into the commit. `-u` remembers the upstream so later `git push` and `git pull` need no arguments.

steps.title: Start SHOP-142 from a fresh main
prompt: `~/shop` is your clone of the team repo (`origin` is `/srv/git/shop.git`). It is a day old: Priya pushed to `main` overnight. You already started editing on your stale `main`: a new `src/Coupon.cs`, a change in `src/Cart.cs`, and an unrelated typo fix in `README.md`.
1. Fetch, and create `feature/SHOP-142-coupons` from the **fresh** `origin/main`, bringing your edits along. Give it no upstream yet (`--no-track`): it should not track `main`.
2. Commit only the coupon work (`src/Coupon.cs`, `src/Cart.cs`) as `Add percentage coupons (SHOP-142)`. The README typo stays uncommitted: it goes into its own small PR later.
3. Publish the branch and set its upstream, so later `git push` and `git pull` need no arguments.

checks.name: the branch starts from the fresh main
checks.fail: `feature/SHOP-142-coupons` should be one commit on top of Priya's newest `main`. `git fetch`, then `git switch -c feature/SHOP-142-coupons --no-track origin/main`.

checks.name: the commit holds the coupon work only
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git log -1 --format=%s feature/SHOP-142-coupons)" = 'Add percentage coupons (SHOP-142)' && test "$(git diff --name-only feature/SHOP-142-coupons^ feature/SHOP-142-coupons | sort | tr '\n' ' ')" = 'src/Cart.cs src/Coupon.cs '
checks.fail: The commit should be `Add percentage coupons (SHOP-142)` and change exactly `src/Cart.cs` and `src/Coupon.cs`.

checks.name: the README typo fix is still uncommitted
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && git diff --name-only | grep -qx README.md && grep -q Welcome README.md
checks.fail: The README fix should still be an uncommitted change in the working tree.

checks.name: pushed, with the upstream set
checks.cmd: cd ~/shop && test "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref feature/SHOP-142-coupons@{upstream})" = origin/feature/SHOP-142-coupons && test "$(git -C /srv/git/shop.git rev-parse feature/SHOP-142-coupons)" = "$(git rev-parse feature/SHOP-142-coupons)"
checks.fail: Push with `git push -u origin HEAD`: the server should have the branch, and its upstream should be `origin/feature/SHOP-142-coupons`.

hints: `git fetch` first; `git log --oneline main..origin/main` shows what Priya pushed.
`git switch -c feature/SHOP-142-coupons --no-track origin/main` carries your uncommitted edits along, because Priya did not touch those files.
`git add src/Coupon.cs src/Cart.cs`, `git commit -m "Add percentage coupons (SHOP-142)"`, `git push -u origin HEAD`.
steps.explain: Branching from `origin/main` right after a fetch means you start on what the team actually has, not on yesterday's copy, and you never needed to update local `main` at all. `--no-track` matters: without it the new branch would track `origin/main`, and a later bare `git push` could aim at the wrong place. `git config --global push.autoSetupRemote true` makes the first `git push` set the upstream by itself.
